Your five questions, answeredVos cinq questions, avec réponses

1 · How many people use a mobile phone?
ESTIMATE
About 8,941,164 of 14,421,233 residents in Rwanda (assuming 62% use a phone). Largest regions: Kinyinya (≈91,924 at 17:00–18:00), Bumbogo (≈75,664 at 17:00–18:00), Karangazi (≈65,296 at 18:00–19:00).
2 · When are most people calling, and where?
ASSUMED HOURS
The call peak is 18:00–19:00 (≈2,365,514 people on a call). Business-like regions peak in office hours, residential regions in the evening — see the heat-map in section 8b. Strongest region: Kinyinya.
3 · When are most cars on the road, and on which roads?
MODELED
Most cars at 07:00–08:00; worst delay at 07:00–08:00; jam windows 07:00–09:00 and 17:00–18:00. Most loaded roads: Link Bumbogo – Jali (v/c 4.44 at 07:00–08:00, both equally), Link Jali – Gahanga (v/c 4.21 at 07:00–08:00, both equally), Link Gahanga – Bumbogo (v/c 3.91 at 07:00–08:00, both equally).
4 · If a road is jammed, which other road can I use?
MODELED
If Link Bigogwe – Nyabirasi is jammed, the best alternative is Link Muhanda – Muzo (would jam too). For Bigogwe → Nyabirasi: detour ≈ 292 min via Link Bigogwe – Muzo → Link Muhanda – Muzo → Link Nyabirasi – Muhanda, instead of ≈ 3409 min on the jammed road. Try your own trip with route_if_jammed(from, to, road).
5 · How good are both networks (signal)?
MEASURED
Mobile: 28.3 Mbps (Good, 4/5 bars) · Fixed: 44.1 Mbps (Good, 4/5 bars). See the signal cards in section 8c for every region.

Prototype scorecard (concept §30)Bilan du prototype

All evidence is simulated: a pass shows the pipeline works, not real-world accuracy.Preuves simulées.
criterion status evidence evidence type
A registered mobile device can securely transmit GPS observations Pass (API self-test) Validation, device token and role checks tested in B12; TLS and per-device tokens still to deploy API
Each observation can be associated with an authorized vehicle Pass 100% of observations resolve to a consenting device and vehicle synthetic
The platform can map-match observations to road segments Pass 100.0% correct on moving points, 100.0% matched (optimistic: simulator follows OSM exactly) synthetic
The dashboard can display participating vehicles in near real time Partial Fleet map shows vehicles, congestion, incident and routes; near-real-time refresh needs the API + WebSocket synthetic
The system can calculate road-level average speed Pass 83 segments with space-mean speed in the last 5 min synthetic
The system can identify current congestion using calibrated rules Fail staged incident missed; thresholds are placeholders until calibrated locally synthetic
An eligible public vehicle can be shown to a passenger with an ETA Pass 8 bus(es) listed; ETA error 5.1 min synthetic
The platform can generate a route recommendation using current traffic Pass 3 options now, 3 at +15 min synthetic
Historical observations can be stored for future ML training Partial 150 segments × 14 days of 5-min aggregates and the schema exist; real history must accumulate (simulated here) synthetic
A pilot sensor can be added without redesigning the core platform Pass 5 sensors of 4 vendor formats enter through one adapter synthetic

Data notesNotes sur les données

  • Ookla: mobile quarters 2024-Q3 → 2026-Q2 (8 quarters); services: mobile, fixed.
  • Population: WorldPop rwa_pop_2025_CN_1km_R2025A_UA_v1.tif; total in study area = 14,421,233.

Parameters used in this run — editableParamètres de ce calcul — modifiables

GlossaryGlossaire

  • v/c: volume ÷ capacity; 1.0 = full road
  • UE / SO: user equilibrium (selfish drivers) / system optimum (coordinated)
  • Gini: 0 = equal speed for all residents, 1 = extreme inequality
  • Digital-divide index: 1 − (median speed in the least-dense class ÷ in the densest class)
  • Gravity model: trips between zones ∝ attraction × exp(−β × travel minutes)
Speed tests are self-selected: no tile = no test, not no coverage. Traffic results are relative indicators; calibrate with RTDA / City of Kigali counts or operator MPD before operational decisions.
